events.what: Joshi claims that his Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces construction, combined with Mochizuki's IUT, proves the abc conjecture and answers every Scholze-Stix objection
events.credibility_reason: F5: it restates a decade-old dispute rather than advancing it. The experts concerned (Scholze) reject it. No journal or expert has taken it up in over two years on a landmark problem. The 2026 LANA formalisation project explicitly declines to conclude that IUT is a valid proof. JUDGE.md F5 names this exact case.

events.what: Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teräväinen improve the bound on the number of exceptional abc triples in a cube of side N from O(N^(2/3)) to O(N^(33/50))
LANA project (ZEN University) Lean formalisation effort on IUT; the July 2026 interim report narrows the disputed step without reaching a conclusion

judgement.doubts: The 2026-09-24 hand correction to progress is right, and it matches JUDGE.md F5, which names Joshi on IUT explicitly. The BBLT result counts as a bound: the bullet asks for finitely many exceptions, and a smaller count of exceptions up to N does not settle that. The ai.basis_quote comes from the LANA project page, not from the BBLT paper the status rests on. It still supports ai_role none, and the record reports no AI in BBLT (the linear program there is solved in Python, which is not AI), so I have left the quote in place. arXiv 2505.13991 ('true almost always') is described only as a survey of density results, so I have not treated it as an event.

corrections.why: F8: the quote is about the LANA formalisation project, not the BBLT paper the status rests on. The record says BBLT used classical analytic number theory plus a linear program solved in Python, with no AI, so ai_role none still holds. I have kept the quote so no evidence is deleted.
